name: Hollow Wretch
loreTies: A small Gateborn husk formed from erased memory. It attacks in groups and leaves cold silence behind when destroyed.
Rushes isolated Deities and punishes careless positioning.
shortBackstory: Hollow Wretch is a non-playable Hollow Creature whose origin makes The First Reopening visible as living battlefield danger.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.text: Hollow Wretch formed where the Gate consumed names faster than the Codex could preserve them. It is not a faction citizen and should never read like a recruitable Deity. Its existence proves that the Gate crisis produces consequences, predators, remnants, and catastrophes beyond civilized armies.

chapters.title: Lore Function
chapters.text: As a Hollow Creature from Hollow, Hollow carries a specific warning into the story: A small Gateborn husk formed from erased memory. It attacks in groups and leaves cold silence behind when destroyed. This makes the creature useful as canon pressure, not random enemy dressing.

chapters.title: Battlefield Behavior
chapters.text: On the map, Hollow supports its lore through behavior: Rushes isolated Deities and punishes careless positioning. Its abilities — Scratch of Forgetting, Swarm Pressure — should feel like the environment and story acting through a threat body.

chapters.title: Campaign Tie
chapters.text: In The First Reopening, Hollow connects to the first proof that erased memory can return as hostile pressure. Encounter designers can place it where the player needs to feel what the Gate has damaged: memory, structure, instinct, oath, water, stone, or command.

chapters.title: Visual / Reading Rule
chapters.text: The creature page must preserve the distinction between Deities, NPCs, and non-playable threats. Hollow can be studied under Creatures and Backstories, but its profile should reinforce danger, not companionship.

developmentStatus: Readable creature profile integrated into dashboard threat pages.
